title: AWL Sublist 10
description: Las 30 palabras de la sublista 10 de la Academic Word List, con definición, traducción, ejemplo académico, colocaciones y familia léxica.

cards.definition: Next to or very near something else.
cards.example: The new library will be built on the land adjacent to the main campus.
cards.warning: Preposición: "adjacent TO". Muy útil en IELTS Task 1 de mapas.

cards.definition: Although; used to add a fact that slightly reduces the force of what was said.
cards.example: Unemployment fell in 2023, albeit at a slower rate than in previous years.
cards.warning: Va seguido de un adjetivo, adverbio o frase corta, no de una oración completa: "albeit slowly", no "albeit it was slow".

cards.definition: To gather people or things together in one place; to fit parts together.
cards.example: The researchers assembled a large database of hospital records.

cards.definition: To fall down suddenly; to fail or stop working completely.
cards.example: The collapse of the fishing industry left many coastal towns without work.
cards.warning: Un "colapso" de tráfico es "a traffic jam" o "gridlock", no "collapse".

cards.definition: A person you work with, especially in a profession or organisation.
cards.example: Darwin discussed his early ideas with only a few trusted colleagues.
cards.warning: "Colega" como amigo informal es "mate" o "buddy", no "colleague".

cards.definition: To collect information from different sources and arrange it in a list, book or report.
cards.example: The data were compiled from national census records.

cards.definition: To form an idea or plan in your mind; to imagine; to become pregnant.
cards.example: The project was originally conceived as a small local initiative.

cards.definition: To make someone believe something is true or persuade them to do something.
cards.example: The minister failed to convince voters that the tax rise was necessary.

cards.definition: To make someone feel sad; to reduce the level or value of something, such as prices.
cards.example: A surplus of cheap imports depressed local wages.
cards.warning: "Depressed" (persona deprimida) vs "depressing" (algo deprimente). "The Great Depression" = la Gran Depresión de 1929.

cards.definition: To experience or meet something, especially a problem or difficulty; a meeting.
cards.example: International students often encounter difficulties finding accommodation.
cards.warning: Para "encontrar" algo que buscas usa "find"; "encounter" es toparse con algo (normalmente un problema).

cards.definition: Extremely large in size or amount.
cards.example: The internet has had an enormous impact on how students learn.
cards.warning: "Enormity" significa "gravedad, atrocidad", no solo "tamaño enorme".

cards.definition: Happening soon; available when needed; willing to give information.
cards.example: Details of the scheme will be published in a forthcoming report.
cards.warning: "Funding was not forthcoming" = no llegó la financiación.

cards.definition: To tend to think or behave in a particular way; a slope.
cards.example: I am inclined to agree that university education should be free.
cards.warning: "I'm inclined to think/agree" es una forma elegante de dar tu opinión con cautela.

cards.definition: The quality of being honest and having strong moral principles; being whole and undamaged.
cards.example: Plagiarism undermines the integrity of academic research.

cards.definition: Belonging naturally to something as part of its basic nature.
cards.example: Students with intrinsic motivation tend to learn more deeply than those seeking rewards.
cards.warning: Su opuesto es "extrinsic" (extrínseco).

cards.definition: To use a law, principle or argument to support a decision; to mention as authority.
cards.example: The government invoked national security to justify the new surveillance law.

cards.definition: An official tax or charge; to officially demand payment of a tax.
cards.example: A levy on sugary drinks was introduced to fund school sports programmes.

cards.definition: In the same way; also.
cards.example: Germany invested heavily in solar energy; likewise, Spain expanded its wind farms.
cards.warning: Conector de comparación/semejanza; alterna con "Similarly".

cards.definition: Despite what has just been said; nevertheless.
cards.example: The plan is expensive. Nonetheless, it offers the best long-term solution.
cards.warning: Se escribe en una sola palabra: "nonetheless", no "none the less" (forma antigua).

cards.definition: Despite something (very formal).
cards.example: Notwithstanding its high cost, the scheme has been widely praised.
cards.warning: Muy formal: puede ir antes o después del sustantivo ("these problems notwithstanding"). No lo fuerces: "despite" suele sonar más natural.

cards.definition: Strange or unusual; (of numbers) not divisible by two; occasional.
cards.example: It seems odd that such an important study received so little attention.
cards.warning: "Odds" = probabilidades: "the odds of success". "Odd number" = número impar (par = "even").

cards.definition: Continuing to exist or develop; still in progress.
cards.example: There is an ongoing debate about the value of standardised testing.
cards.warning: Suele ir delante del sustantivo ("ongoing research"), pero también tras "be": "the investigation is ongoing" (= sigue en curso).

cards.definition: A group of experts who discuss or judge something; a flat piece of material.
cards.example: An independent panel of experts reviewed the safety data.

cards.definition: To continue to exist; to keep trying to do something despite difficulties.
cards.example: Gender pay gaps persist in almost every industry.

cards.definition: To create a problem or threat; to ask a question.
cards.example: Rising sea levels pose a serious threat to low-lying islands.
cards.warning: Colocación clave para Writing: "pose a threat/risk/challenge" (no "make a threat" en este sentido).

cards.definition: Unwillingness to do something.
cards.example: Many farmers show reluctance to adopt new technologies because of the costs.
cards.warning: Se construye con "to + infinitive": "reluctant to change".

cards.definition: Used to show the name commonly given to something, sometimes when you doubt it is accurate.
cards.example: The so-called 'gig economy' offers flexibility but little job security.
cards.warning: A veces tiene matiz irónico o de duda ("so-called experts" = supuestos expertos).

cards.definition: Easy to understand or do; honest and direct.
cards.example: There is no straightforward solution to the problem of traffic congestion.

cards.definition: To experience something, especially a change or something unpleasant.
cards.example: The city centre has undergone major changes over the past twenty years.
cards.warning: Irregular: undergo - underwent - undergone. Muy útil en IELTS Task 1 de mapas ("the area underwent...").

cards.definition: By which; through which (used to describe a system or method).
cards.es: por el cual, mediante el cual
cards.example: The company introduced a scheme whereby employees can work from home two days a week.
cards.warning: Sustituye a "by which" tras sustantivos como "system", "process" o "scheme".
